headline: I Am Now Paying A 'Pavement Depreciation Fee' Every Time I Walk To The Grocery Store
body:
I used to think my morning walk to the local kirana store was a simple act of necessity, but as of this morning, it is a taxable event. I was stopped at the corner of 4th Cross by a municipal contractor who informed me that my rubber-soled sandals were causing 'micro-abrasions' on the public footpath, and therefore, I owe the city a flat fee of fifty rupees for the wear-and-tear I am inflicting on the concrete.

He pulled out a handheld thermal printer, clicked a few buttons labeled 'Moderate Stride' and 'Leisurely Pace,' and handed me a receipt that smelled faintly of burnt plastic. Apparently, the city’s new plan to turn every square inch of Bengaluru into a revenue-generating asset means that simply existing on the sidewalk now requires a micro-transaction. I tried to explain that I was just going to buy milk, but the official pointed out that my trajectory showed I intended to use the curb as well, which is an 'Advanced Surface Usage' premium.

It’s getting complicated to leave my house without a tax consultant. I’ve started calculating the most cost-effective route to the bus stop, trying to avoid high-friction zones and public seating areas that cost extra by the minute. Yesterday, I accidentally leaned against a lamppost while waiting for an auto and received a notification on my phone that I had been docked ten rupees for 'Unauthorized Structural Support.' I’m considering buying a pair of hover-shoes, though I suspect the city will just invent a 'Gravity Interference' levy to cover that too.
caption: Living in the city has become a choose-your-own-adventure game where every move costs extra. Are you also getting taxed for just existing on the sidewalk? #Bengaluru #CivicLife #ParkingTax #UrbanLiving (satire)
